introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0770 Pure Maths With Statistics 1, June 2023, Advanced Level, one and a half hours). Answer ALL questions: Section A is Pure Mathematics (questions 1 to 35) and Section B is Statistics (questions 36 to 50). Formulae booklets and calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer you score zero). Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.

figures.legende: Venn diagram with sets X, Y, Z inside the universal set; the region inside Y and Z but outside X is shaded.

incertitudes: Le sujet est un scan sans couche texte (6 pages, filigranes gcerevision.com ignorés), lu page par page en image puis relu en recadrages agrandis. Aucun corrigé ni clé officiels : tous les corrigés sont rédigés et chaque valeur numérique recalculée par script (sympy absent, calculs Python/numpy et fractions exactes). Aucune constante physique n'est nécessaire. Le sujet compte bien 50 questions (35 de Pure Mathematics, 15 de Statistics).

Question 12 : la définition imprimée n'est pas strictement cohérente (les deux branches contiennent x = 2, donnant 4 et 13, et f(3) = 28 est différent de f(0) = 0 alors que la période est 3) ; la réponse A (f(9) = f(0) = 0) est la seule option compatible avec la réduction modulo 3, elle est conservée.
Question 18 : le logarithme est pris en base 10 (en base e le résultat, environ 6,91, n'est dans aucune option).

Question 27 : la réponse dépend du diagramme de Venn (figure recadrée depuis le scan, fig-1) ; la région hachurée est lue comme X' inter Y inter Z, c'est-à-dire la partie de Y inter Z située en dehors de X.
Question 38 : la covariance est calculée avec le diviseur n (résultat -2,25, option D) ; avec n - 1 on obtiendrait -3, absent des options.
Question 40 : l'énoncé imprimé porte « (X) = 1,6 » (le mot Var est tombé à la coupure de ligne dans le scan) ; lu comme Var(X) = 1,6, ce qui donne n = 10, option D.
Question 45 : le sujet note S_x^2, S_y^2 et S_xy sans préciser le diviseur ; le coefficient r = S_xy / racine(S_x^2 S_y^2) = 0,98 ne dépend pas du diviseur s'il est le même pour les trois (option A).
Question 46 : la densité est décroissante sur tout l'intervalle [2, 4] ; le mode est donc l'extrémité gauche x = 2 (option D), et non le sommet de la parabole intérieur à l'intervalle.
Question 43 (statistique) : le sujet n'imprime AUCUNE option de réponse ; la question est transcrite directement comme question ouverte, réponse 6,98 (48,875 / 7 = 6,982).

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 2, 30, 50. Question 2 : la valeur exacte g(f(-1)) = 19/2 est absente des options imprimées (A et B sont toutes deux imprimées 19/3, C 7/2, D -3). Question 30 : la règle des trapèzes (6 ordonnées, h = 2) donne 20,6, absent des options (19,2 ; 11,3 ; 12,1 ; 18,8) ; la table a été relue à fort grossissement (0,3 ; 0,8 ; 1,6 ; 2,4 ; 2,7 ; 5,3). Question 50 : avec correction de continuité, P(X > 30) = P(Z > 2,625), absent des options (1,88 ; 2,52 ; 1,86 ; 2,50) ; seule l'option D (2,50) correspond à l'approximation sans correction de continuité, et aucune clé n'est affirmée.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION A: PURE MATHEMATICS**

Given that $4^{3x+2}=2^{6+2x}$, the value of $x$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Write both sides with base $2$: $4^{3x+2}=(2^2)^{3x+2}=2^{6x+4}$. Equating the exponents, $6x+4=6+2x$, so $4x=2$ and $x=\dfrac12$. Check: $4^{3.5}=2^{7}=128$ and $2^{6+1}=2^{7}=128$. Option D comes from doubling only the $3x$ and forgetting to double the $2$ (giving $2^{6x+2}$, hence $x=1$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two functions $f$ and $g$ are defined on the set of real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ by $f(x)=2-3x$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{4x-1}{2}$, $g\circ f(-1)=$

*Options as printed:* A) $\dfrac{19}{3}$   B) $\dfrac{19}{3}$   C) $\dfrac{7}{2}$   D) $-3$
questions.corrige_markdown:
$g\circ f(-1)=g\big(f(-1)\big)$. First $f(-1)=2-3(-1)=5$. Then $g(5)=\dfrac{4(5)-1}{2}=\dfrac{19}{2}$. The correct value $\dfrac{19}{2}=9.5$ is not among the printed options (A and B are both printed as $\dfrac{19}{3}$, C is $\dfrac72$, D is $-3$), so the question cannot be marked automatically.

**Answer: $\dfrac{19}{2}$ (not listed).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Two statements $p$ and $q$ are logically equivalent if
questions.corrige_markdown: Two statements are logically equivalent, written $p\equiv q$, exactly when they take the same truth value in every possible case, that is, when their truth tables are identical (equivalently $p\Leftrightarrow q$ is a tautology). A describes only a special case (two contradictions are equivalent, but so are two tautologies and many other pairs), not the general condition. B is meaningless: any two statements can be linked by an operator, for instance $p\wedge q$ and $p\vee q$ are not equivalent. D confuses equivalence with the converse of an implication: $q\Rightarrow p$ is not logically equivalent to $p\Rightarrow q$. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: $p$ and $q$ are linked by a logic operator

questions.enonce_markdown: If $\dfrac{x-5}{1-x^2}\equiv\dfrac{M}{1+x}+\dfrac{N}{1-x}$, then
questions.corrige_markdown: Multiply by $1-x^2=(1+x)(1-x)$: $x-5\equiv M(1-x)+N(1+x)$. Put $x=-1$: $-6=2M$, so $M=-3$. Put $x=1$: $-4=2N$, so $N=-2$. Check by recombining: $\dfrac{-3(1-x)-2(1+x)}{1-x^2}=\dfrac{-5+x}{1-x^2}$. Options A, C and D each change at least one sign, which fails the check. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of $t$ for which the plane $2x+4y+tz=9$ and the line $\mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}+9\mathbf{k}+\lambda(3\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k})$ are parallel is
questions.corrige_markdown: A line with direction $\mathbf{d}=(3,-5,2)$ is parallel to a plane with normal $\mathbf{n}=(2,4,t)$ exactly when $\mathbf{d}\cdot\mathbf{n}=0$ (the line is perpendicular to the normal). So $6-20+2t=0$, giving $t=7$. The line is then parallel but not inside the plane: the point $(2,4,9)$ gives $4+16+63=83\neq 9$. Setting $\mathbf d$ proportional to $\mathbf n$ (the condition for a line perpendicular to the plane) is the usual wrong turn. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Cartesian equation of the curve with parametric equation $x=1+\sin\theta$, $y=2-\cos\theta$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Isolate $\sin\theta=x-1$ and $\cos\theta=2-y$, then use $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $(x-1)^2+(y-2)^2=1$. Expanding, $x^2-2x+1+y^2-4y+4=1$, that is $x^2+y^2-2x-4y+4=0$: a circle of centre $(1,2)$ and radius $1$. Option C has the wrong constant ($-4$ would give radius $3$) and D has the wrong sign on $y$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The third term in the binomial expansion of $(1-4x)^{-6}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: For a negative index, $(1+u)^{n}=1+nu+\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}u^2+\cdots$ with $n=-6$ and $u=-4x$. The third term is $\dfrac{(-6)(-7)}{2}(-4x)^2=21\cdot16x^2=336x^2$. It contains $x^2$ (the third term is the term in $u^2$, not $u^3$) and the sign is positive because $(-4x)^2>0$ and $(-6)(-7)>0$. The expansion is valid for $|x|<\tfrac14$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The general solution of the differential equation $(1+x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Separate the variables: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$, so $y=2\int\dfrac{dx}{1+x^2}=2\tan^{-1}x+A$. The answers with $\dfrac{x}{2}$ misapply $\int\dfrac{dx}{a^2+x^2}=\dfrac1a\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}$ with $a=2$, but the denominator here is $1+x^2$ (so $a=1$) and the $2$ is a constant factor. Differentiating option A: $2\cdot\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$, which is the required derivative. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: All the asymptotes of the graph of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{5x^2+3}{(x+2)(x-1)}$ are
questions.corrige_markdown: Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator vanishes and the numerator does not: $x=-2$ (numerator $5\cdot4+3=23$) and $x=1$ (numerator $8$). The numerator and denominator have the same degree $2$, so the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of the leading coefficients: $y=\dfrac{5}{1}=5$ (check: $f(x)=\dfrac{5+3/x^2}{1+1/x-2/x^2}\to5$). The other options take the roots of the denominator with the wrong sign. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of $m$ for which $\begin{vmatrix}3&m&-1\\1&-1&3\\2&0&2\end{vmatrix}=-2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Expand along the first row: $3\big[(-1)(2)-(3)(0)\big]-m\big[(1)(2)-(3)(2)\big]+(-1)\big[(1)(0)-(-1)(2)\big]=3(-2)-m(-4)-(2)=4m-8$. Setting $4m-8=-2$ gives $m=\dfrac{6}{4}=\dfrac32$. Check: with $m=1.5$ the determinant is $-2$. Forgetting the minus sign in front of the middle cofactor is the usual error. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The range of values of $x$ for which $(3-x)(7+x)\le0$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The roots are $x=3$ and $x=-7$. Since $(3-x)(7+x)=-(x-3)(x+7)$, the inequality $\le0$ is equivalent to $(x-3)(x+7)\ge0$, an upward parabola, which is non-negative outside the roots: $x\le-7$ or $x\ge3$. The roots are included because the inequality is not strict (at $x=-7$ the product is $0$), which rules out B. D describes the interval where the product is positive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A function $f$ defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}2x, & 0\le x\le2,\\ 3x^2+1, & 2\le x\le3,\end{cases}$ is periodic with period $3$. $f(9)=$
questions.corrige_markdown: Periodicity with period $3$ means $f(x+3)=f(x)$, so $f(9)=f(6)=f(3)=f(0)$, since $9=3\times3+0$. Hence $f(9)=f(0)=2(0)=0$. Only this reduction modulo $3$ to $x=0$ gives an option ($0$). (The printed definition is not strictly consistent: both branches claim $x=2$, giving $4$ and $13$, and $f(3)=28\ne f(0)$; the intended answer is the value at $0$.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The remainder when $x^3-3x^2-4x-12$ is divided by $x+2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: By the remainder theorem the remainder on division by $x+2=x-(-2)$ is $P(-2)$: $(-2)^3-3(-2)^2-4(-2)-12=-8-12+8-12=-24$. Evaluating at $x=+2$ instead (the usual slip) also happens to give $8-12-8-12=-24$ here, but the sign of the root matters in general. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The eighth term of a geometric progression is $256$ and the first term is $2$. The common ratio is
questions.corrige_markdown: The $n$th term is $ar^{n-1}$. So $ar^{7}=2r^7=256$, giving $r^7=128=2^7$ and $r=2$. Option B is the value of $r^7$, not of $r$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of arrangements of the letters of the word $ARREARS$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $ARREARS$ has $7$ letters: $A$ twice, $R$ three times, $E$ once, $S$ once. The number of distinct arrangements is $\dfrac{7!}{2!\,3!}=\dfrac{5040}{12}=420$. Dividing by $3!$ only (forgetting the repeated $A$) gives $840$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Cartesian equation of the plane containing the point $\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}-8\mathbf{k}$ and perpendicular to the line $\mathbf{r}=3\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}+t(5\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}-4\mathbf{k})$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: A plane perpendicular to a line has the direction of the line as its normal: $\mathbf n=(5,-1,-4)$, so the plane is $5x-y-4z=d$. The point $(1,3,-8)$ lies on it: $d=5(1)-3-4(-8)=5-3+32=34$. The plane is $5x-y-4z=34$. A, B and C have normals $(5,-1,4)$, $(5,1,-4)$ and $(-5,1,-4)$, none of which is parallel to the line direction $(5,-1,-4)$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&1&5\\-1&2&3\\4&1&7\end{pmatrix}$, the cofactor of $7$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The entry $7$ is in row $3$, column $3$. Its cofactor is $(-1)^{3+3}$ times the minor obtained by deleting row $3$ and column $3$: $+\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\-1&2\end{vmatrix}=2\cdot2-1\cdot(-1)=4+1=5$. Using $2\cdot2-1\cdot1=3$ (missing the sign of $-1$) leads to option A. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $\log24-\dfrac12\log9+\log125=$
questions.corrige_markdown: Taking $\log$ to base $10$: $\dfrac12\log9=\log9^{1/2}=\log3$. So the expression is $\log24-\log3+\log125=\log\dfrac{24\times125}{3}=\log(8\times125)=\log1000=3$. (A natural logarithm would give $\ln1000\approx6.91$, which is not an option, so base $10$ is intended.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $\sin\theta=\dfrac12$, the values of $\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi$, are
questions.corrige_markdown: The principal value is $\theta=\sin^{-1}\dfrac12=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$. In $0<\theta<\pi$ the sine is also positive in the second quadrant, with $\theta=\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$. Check: $\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}=\dfrac12$. In options B, C and D the sines are $1$, $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ or $\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$, never $\dfrac12$ for both angles. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The vector equations of $4$ straight lines $L_1,L_2,L_3,L_4$ are given by: $L_1:\ \mathbf r=3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+4\mathbf k+\lambda_1(4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)$, $L_2:\ \mathbf r=\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+\mathbf k+\lambda_2(8\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-6\mathbf k)$, $L_3:\ \mathbf r=2\mathbf i+6\mathbf j+2\mathbf k+\lambda_3(\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+4\mathbf k)$, $L_4:\ \mathbf r=4\mathbf i+12\mathbf j+4\mathbf k+\lambda_4(3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+\mathbf k)$. The parallel pair of lines is
questions.corrige_markdown: Two lines are parallel when their direction vectors are proportional. The directions are $\mathbf d_1=(4,2,-3)$, $\mathbf d_2=(8,4,-6)=2\mathbf d_1$, $\mathbf d_3=(1,-4,4)$, $\mathbf d_4=(3,-1,1)$. Only $\mathbf d_1$ and $\mathbf d_2$ are proportional; every other pair has a non-zero cross product (for example $\mathbf d_3\times\mathbf d_4=(0,11,11)$). The lines are distinct (not coincident) because the join of base points $(3,-2,4)$ and $(1,3,1)$ is $(2,-5,3)$, which is not a multiple of $\mathbf d_1$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}4\beta+4x & \text{if } x<1,\\ 4x-\beta^2-4 & \text{if } x>1.\end{cases}$ If $f$ has a limit as $x\to1$, the value of the constant $\beta$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The limit exists when the left-hand and right-hand limits are equal. As $x\to1^-$, $f(x)\to4\beta+4$; as $x\to1^+$, $f(x)\to4-\beta^2-4=-\beta^2$. Equating, $4\beta+4=-\beta^2$, so $\beta^2+4\beta+4=0$, that is $(\beta+2)^2=0$ and $\beta=-2$ (a repeated root). Check: both one-sided limits equal $-4$. The value $f(1)$ plays no role in the existence of a limit. **Answer: D.**

With $i^2=-1$ and $i^4=1$: numerator $2+i-1=1+i$; denominator $i-1+1=i$. Then $\dfrac{1+i}{i}=\dfrac{(1+i)(-i)}{i(-i)}=\dfrac{-i-i^2}{1}=-i+1=1-i$. Check: $(1-i)\cdot i=i-i^2=1+i$. Option B comes from multiplying by $i$ instead of dividing. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A relation $R$ defined on a non-empty set $S$ is called a partial order if $R$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: By definition, a partial order is a relation that is reflexive ($aRa$), anti-symmetric ($aRb$ and $bRa$ imply $a=b$) and transitive. Option C describes an equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive). Options A and D include symmetry, which together with anti-symmetry reduces $R$ to the identity relation (a trivial case, not the definition), and D also omits reflexivity. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $(\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)\times(-2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+\mathbf k)=$
questions.corrige_markdown: Expand $\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&2&2\\-2&3&1\end{vmatrix}=\mathbf i(2\cdot1-2\cdot3)-\mathbf j(1\cdot1-2\cdot(-2))+\mathbf k(1\cdot3-2\cdot(-2))=-4\mathbf i-5\mathbf j+7\mathbf k$. Check: the result is perpendicular to both vectors: $(1,2,2)\cdot(-4,-5,7)=-4-10+14=0$ and $(-2,3,1)\cdot(-4,-5,7)=8-15+7=0$. The middle term carries a minus sign, which is the usual slip (options B and D). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $\sin\theta-\sqrt3\cos\theta=R\sin(\theta-\lambda)$, where $R>0$ and $\lambda$ is an acute angle, $R$ and $\lambda$ are such that
questions.corrige_markdown: Expand: $R\sin(\theta-\lambda)=R\cos\lambda\,\sin\theta-R\sin\lambda\,\cos\theta$. Matching coefficients, $R\cos\lambda=1$ and $R\sin\lambda=\sqrt3$. Hence $R=\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt3)^2}=2$ and $\tan\lambda=\sqrt3$, so $\lambda=60^\circ$ (acute). The value $\sqrt{10}$ would come from squaring $3$ instead of $\sqrt3$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The roots of the equation $2x^2-3x-1=0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$. The equation whose roots are $2\alpha+1$ and $2\beta+1$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: From $2x^2-3x-1=0$: $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac32$ and $\alpha\beta=-\dfrac12$. New sum: $(2\alpha+1)+(2\beta+1)=2(\alpha+\beta)+2=3+2=5$. New product: $(2\alpha+1)(2\beta+1)=4\alpha\beta+2(\alpha+\beta)+1=-2+3+1=2$. The equation is $x^2-(\text{sum})x+(\text{product})=0$, that is $x^2-5x+2=0$. Numerical check: $\alpha\approx1.781$, $\beta\approx-0.281$, new roots $4.562$ and $0.438$, sum $5$, product $2$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-al-pm-statistics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

The set represented by the shaded region is
questions.corrige_markdown: In the Venn diagram (universal set $\mathcal U$ with sets $X$, $Y$, $Z$), the shaded region lies inside both $Y$ and $Z$ but outside $X$: it is the part of the lens $Y\cap Z$ that does not meet $X$. So the set is $X'\cap Y\cap Z$. Option B, $Y\cap Z$, also contains the part of the lens inside $X$ (that is $X\cap Y\cap Z$). Option C equals $Y\cap Z$ again because $X\cap Y\cap Z\subseteq Y\cap Z$ (absorption). Option D is outside both $Y$ and $Z$, so it cannot be the shaded region. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The relationship between the logarithms of the variables $x$ and $y$ which are connected by $2y+10=ab^{(x-3)}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Take logarithms (any base) of both sides and use $\log(PQ)=\log P+\log Q$ and $\log P^k=k\log P$: $\log(2y+10)=\log a+\log b^{x-3}=\log a+(x-3)\log b$. This is linear in $x$ with gradient $\log b$ (a straight line when $\log(2y+10)$ is plotted against $x$). Option C wrongly multiplies $\log a$ by $(x-3)$; A and D wrongly subtract. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression is $S_n$, where $S_n=n(2n+3)$. The $n^{th}$ term of the progression is
questions.corrige_markdown: The $n$th term is $u_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$ for $n\ge2$: $S_n=2n^2+3n$ and $S_{n-1}=2(n-1)^2+3(n-1)=2n^2-n-1$, so $u_n=(2n^2+3n)-(2n^2-n-1)=4n+1$. For $n=1$: $u_1=S_1=5=4(1)+1$, so the formula holds for all $n$. The progression has first term $5$ and common difference $4$. Check: $S_3=3\cdot9=27=5+9+13$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The values of $y$ corresponding to values of $x$ in an experiment are given on the table below.

| $x$ | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $y$ | 0.3 | 0.8 | 1.6 | 2.4 | 2.7 | 5.3 |

Using the trapezium rule, the approximate value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{10}y\,dx$ is

*Options as printed:* A) $19.2$   B) $11.3$   C) $12.1$   D) $18.8$
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trapezium rule with $6$ ordinates ($5$ strips) of width $h=2$: $\displaystyle\int_0^{10}y\,dx\approx\frac h2\Big[y_0+y_5+2(y_1+y_2+y_3+y_4)\Big]=1\times\big[0.3+5.3+2(0.8+1.6+2.4+2.7)\big]=5.6+2(7.5)=5.6+15=20.6$. The correct value $20.6$ is not among the printed options ($19.2$, $11.3$, $12.1$, $18.8$); the question is therefore left open.

**Answer: $20.6$ (not listed).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The first approximation to the root of the equation $x^3-4=0$ is $1.5$. Using the Newton-Raphson method, the second approximation to the root of the equation is
questions.corrige_markdown: Newton-Raphson: $x_{n+1}=x_n-\dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$ with $f(x)=x^3-4$, $f'(x)=3x^2$. With $x_1=1.5$: $f(1.5)=3.375-4=-0.625$ and $f'(1.5)=3(2.25)=6.75$. So $x_2=1.5-\dfrac{-0.625}{6.75}=1.5+0.09259\ldots=1.59259\ldots\approx1.593$ (3 d.p.). (The exact root is $4^{1/3}=1.5874$.) The options differ only in the third decimal place, so careful rounding of $1.5926\ldots$ is needed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest value of $5\sin\theta-12\cos\theta+20$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Write $5\sin\theta-12\cos\theta=R\sin(\theta-\alpha)$ with $R=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=13$. Its greatest value is $13$ (when $\sin(\theta-\alpha)=1$), so the greatest value of the whole expression is $13+20=33$. Option C forgets the $+20$; B is the least-value-type error $-13+20=7$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $z=\sqrt3+i$, $\arg(z^6)=$
questions.corrige_markdown: $|z|=\sqrt{3+1}=2$ and $z$ is in the first quadrant with $\tan(\arg z)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$, so $\arg z=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$. By de Moivre, $z^6=2^6\left(\cos\pi+i\sin\pi\right)=-64$, so $\arg(z^6)=6\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\pi$. Option C is $\arg z$ itself (the exponent was ignored). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $\displaystyle\int 2x(3x^2+5)^7\,dx=$
questions.corrige_markdown: Substitute $u=3x^2+5$, so $du=6x\,dx$ and $2x\,dx=\dfrac13du$. Then $\displaystyle\int2x(3x^2+5)^7dx=\frac13\int u^7du=\frac13\cdot\frac{u^8}{8}+C=\frac{1}{24}(3x^2+5)^8+C$. Check by differentiating: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\dfrac{(3x^2+5)^8}{24}=\dfrac{8(3x^2+5)^7\cdot6x}{24}=2x(3x^2+5)^7$. Options C and D leave a factor of $x$ outside the power, which cannot be integrated that way. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is given by $f(x)=\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{x-2}-3}$, the domain of $f$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: We need $x\neq2$ and $\dfrac{2}{x-2}-3\ge0$, i.e. $\dfrac{2-3(x-2)}{x-2}=\dfrac{8-3x}{x-2}\ge0$. The critical values are $x=2$ and $x=\dfrac83$. For $x<2$: $\dfrac{2}{x-2}<0$ so the radicand is $<-3$, impossible. For $2<x\le\dfrac83$ the quotient is $\ge0$ (equal to $0$ at $x=\dfrac83$, where $\sqrt0=0$ is defined). For $x>\dfrac83$ the numerator is negative and the denominator positive. So the domain is $2<x\le\dfrac83$; $x=2$ is excluded (division by zero). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION B: STATISTICS**

The median of the set of data $3,4,4,6,7,8,9,3,4,7,8,9,3,8,9,4$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: There are $n=16$ values. Arranged in order: $3,3,3,4,4,4,4,6,7,7,8,8,8,9,9,9$. With $n$ even, the median is the mean of the $\dfrac n2=8$th and $9$th values: $\dfrac{6+7}{2}=6.5$. The other options are other averages of this data: the mode is $4$ (option A) and the mean is $\dfrac{96}{16}=6$ (option B). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two independent events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=0.3$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.58$. $P(B)=$
questions.corrige_markdown: Addition rule: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$, and for independent events $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$. Let $p=P(B)$: $0.58=0.3+p-0.3p=0.3+0.7p$, so $p=\dfrac{0.28}{0.7}=0.4$. Check: $P(A\cap B)=0.12$ and $0.3+0.4-0.12=0.58$. Using $P(B)=0.58-0.3=0.28$ treats $A$ and $B$ as mutually exclusive, which contradicts independence. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The set of ordered pairs $\{(x,y)\}$, $\{(4,8),(5,9),(6,6),(7,3)\}$ is such that $\bar x=5.50$ and $\bar y=6.50$. The covariance of the ordered pairs is
questions.corrige_markdown: Covariance (divisor $n=4$): $s_{xy}=\dfrac{\sum xy}{n}-\bar x\,\bar y$. $\sum xy=4\cdot8+5\cdot9+6\cdot6+7\cdot3=32+45+36+21=134$, so $s_{xy}=\dfrac{134}{4}-5.5\times6.5=33.5-35.75=-2.25$. The sign is negative because $y$ tends to fall as $x$ rises. (With divisor $n-1$ the result would be $-3.0$, which is not an option, so the divisor $n$ is the one intended.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A random variable $X$ has cumulative distribution function $F(x)=k(3x-1)$ for $x=1,2,3$. The value of the real constant $k$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: For a discrete random variable taking values $1,2,3$, the cumulative distribution function must reach $1$ at the largest value: $F(3)=k(9-1)=8k=1$, so $k=\dfrac18$. Check: $F(1)=\dfrac28$, $F(2)=\dfrac58$, $F(3)=1$ is increasing, giving $P(X=1)=\dfrac14$, $P(X=2)=\dfrac38$, $P(X=3)=\dfrac38$, which sum to $1$. Forcing $F(1)=1$ would give $k=\dfrac12$, which then makes $F(2)>1$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Random variable $X\sim B(n,p)$. If $E(X)=2$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)=1.6$, the value of $n$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: For $X\sim B(n,p)$: $E(X)=np$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)=npq$ with $q=1-p$. So $np=2$ and $npq=1.6$. Dividing, $q=\dfrac{1.6}{2}=0.8$, so $p=0.2$ and $n=\dfrac{2}{0.2}=10$. Check: $\mathrm{Var}=10(0.2)(0.8)=1.6$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A frequency distribution is such that: Lower quartile $=22.5$, Median $=24.3$ and Upper quartile $=28.7$. The quartile deviation for the distribution is
questions.corrige_markdown: The quartile deviation (semi-interquartile range) is $\dfrac{Q_3-Q_1}{2}=\dfrac{28.7-22.5}{2}=\dfrac{6.2}{2}=3.1$. Option B is the interquartile range $Q_3-Q_1$ (the division by $2$ was forgotten). The median is not needed. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A sample of size $30$ is drawn from an infinite population with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$. The variance of the sample mean is
questions.corrige_markdown: For a random sample of size $n$ from a population of variance $\sigma^2$, $\mathrm{Var}(\bar X)=\dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}$ (and $E(\bar X)=\mu$). With $n=30$: $\dfrac{\sigma^2}{30}$. The population is infinite, so no finite-population correction applies. Options A and B are not variances (the $\sigma$ is not squared); C uses $n-1$, which belongs to the unbiased estimate of $\sigma^2$, not to $\mathrm{Var}(\bar X)$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A sample of size $8$ drawn from a population gives rise to $\sum x=391$, $\sum x^2=19159$. Using this sample, the unbiased estimate of the population variance is

*Options as printed:* none (the source paper prints no answer options for this question).
questions.corrige_markdown:
The unbiased estimate of the population variance from a sample of size $n$ is $s^2=\dfrac{1}{n-1}\left[\sum x^2-\dfrac{\left(\sum x\right)^2}{n}\right]$. Here $\dfrac{(\sum x)^2}{n}=\dfrac{391^2}{8}=\dfrac{152881}{8}=19110.125$, so $\sum x^2-\dfrac{(\sum x)^2}{n}=19159-19110.125=48.875$. Therefore $s^2=\dfrac{48.875}{7}=6.982\ldots\approx6.98$ (3 s.f.). (Dividing by $n=8$ instead of $n-1=7$ would give the biased value $6.11$.)

**Answer: $s^2\approx6.98$.**

The source paper prints no answer options for this question, so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A population has mean $15$ and standard deviation $2.3$. A random sample of size $81$ is taken from the population and its mean is found to be $15.4$. A hypothesis test is to be conducted to verify if the mean has changed. The value of the test statistic for this test is
questions.corrige_markdown: Test $H_0:\mu=15$ against $H_1:\mu\neq15$. The population standard deviation is known and $n=81$ is large, so the test statistic is $Z=\dfrac{\bar x-\mu}{\sigma/\sqrt n}\sim N(0,1)$ under $H_0$. $Z=\dfrac{15.4-15}{2.3/\sqrt{81}}=\dfrac{0.4}{2.3/9}=\dfrac{3.6}{2.3}=1.565$ (3 d.p.). It is positive because $\bar x>\mu$, which excludes B. The values $\pm1.645$ are critical values (one-tailed $5\%$), not a test statistic computed from the data. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For ten pairs of values $(x,y)$, $\bar x=13$, $\bar y=7.08$, $S_x^2=1.246$, $S_y^2=1.611$ and $S_{xy}=1.389$. The product moment correlation coefficient is
questions.corrige_markdown: The product moment correlation coefficient is $r=\dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_x^2\,S_y^2}}$ (the same divisor must be used in the three quantities, in which case it cancels). $r=\dfrac{1.389}{\sqrt{1.246\times1.611}}=\dfrac{1.389}{\sqrt{2.0073}}=\dfrac{1.389}{1.4168}=0.980$ (2 d.p.). This indicates a very strong positive linear correlation ($-1\le r\le1$). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A continuous random variable $X$ has probability density function $f$ given by $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{16}x(4-x)$, $2\le x\le4$. The mode of $X$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The mode of a continuous random variable is the value of $x$ in its range where the density is greatest. $f'(x)=\dfrac{3}{16}(4-2x)$, which is $0$ at $x=2$ and negative for $2<x\le4$, so $f$ is decreasing on the whole range $[2,4]$ and its maximum is at the left end $x=2$, where $f(2)=\dfrac{3}{16}\cdot2\cdot2=0.75$. Check with other values: $f(2.2)=0.7425$, $f(2.4)=0.72$, $f(2.5)=0.703$, all smaller. (The pdf is valid: $\int_2^4f(x)\,dx=1$.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A continuous random variable $X$ has probability density function $g$ given by $g(x)=ax(2-x)$, $0\le x\le2$. The value of the constant $a$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: A probability density function integrates to $1$ over its range: $\displaystyle\int_0^2ax(2-x)\,dx=a\Big[x^2-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\Big]_0^2=a\Big(4-\dfrac83\Big)=\dfrac{4a}{3}=1$, so $a=\dfrac34$. Check: $g(x)\ge0$ on $[0,2]$ with $a=\dfrac34$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A random variable $X\sim\mathrm{Po}(\lambda)$. If $49P(X=0)=8P(X=2)$, the value of the parameter $\lambda$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: For $X\sim\mathrm{Po}(\lambda)$, $P(X=r)=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^r}{r!}$. So $P(X=0)=e^{-\lambda}$ and $P(X=2)=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^2}{2}$. The condition gives $49e^{-\lambda}=8\cdot\dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^2}{2}=4\lambda^2e^{-\lambda}$, so $\lambda^2=\dfrac{49}{4}$ and $\lambda=\dfrac72=3.5$ ($\lambda>0$). Option A is $\lambda^2=12.25$, with the square root forgotten. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For two events $A$ and $B$, $P(A)=\dfrac15$, $P(B)=\dfrac35$, $P(B\mid A)=\dfrac1{10}$. The value of $P(A\cap B)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: By the multiplication rule, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\,P(B\mid A)=\dfrac15\times\dfrac1{10}=\dfrac1{50}$. Option A uses $P(B)\times P(B\mid A)$, the wrong factor. Since $P(B\mid A)\ne P(B)$, the events are not independent, so $P(A)P(B)=\dfrac{3}{25}$ (option C) is not $P(A\cap B)$. **Answer: B.**

themes: normal approximation to the binomial distribution
questions.enonce_markdown:
A discrete random variable $X\sim B(100,0.2)$. Using the normal approximation, $P(X>30)$ is equivalent to

*Options as printed:* A) $P(Z>1.88)$   B) $P(Z>2.52)$   C) $P(Z>1.86)$   D) $P(Z>2.50)$
questions.corrige_markdown:
$X\sim B(100,0.2)$ has mean $np=20$ and variance $npq=100(0.2)(0.8)=16$, so $X$ is approximated by $N(20,\,4^2)$ (valid since $np>5$ and $nq>5$). Because $X$ is discrete, a continuity correction is required: with $Y\sim N(20,16)$: $P(X>30)=P(X\ge31)\approx P(Y>30.5)$, giving $Z=\dfrac{30.5-20}{4}=2.625$, that is $P(Z>2.625)$. This value is not among the printed options. Without the continuity correction the standardised value would be $\dfrac{30-20}{4}=2.50$, which matches only option D, but that omits a step the method requires; none of $1.88$, $2.52$, $1.86$ comes from the data. (For reference the exact binomial value is $P(X>30)\approx0.0061$, while $P(Z>2.625)\approx0.0043$ and $P(Z>2.5)\approx0.0062$.)

**Answer: $P(Z>2.625)$ with the continuity correction (not listed).**
